evals.prompt: I'm trying to debug why my C64 BASIC program isn't getting a response from my API server. The program opens a GET request to my echo server at http://192.168.1.131:8080/echo, sends it, reads the status, but the status line shows 'STATUS: 0' and the serial log doesn't show any 'Request URL:' or 'perform OK' lines. I've flashed the latest firmware. Can you help me diagnose what's going wrong and fix it?
evals.expected_output: A systematic debugging session that: 1) checks serial capture is running, 2) reads the C64 screen, 3) injects a diagnostic program, 4) greps serial logs, 5) diagnoses the issue from evidence, 6) deploys the fix (either BASIC or firmware change)

evals.prompt: I'm working on a C64 chat client that talks to an Ollama API via Meatloaf. The first question works fine — I get a response back. But when I ask a second question (the program loops back and makes another POST request), it just shows the same answer as the first question. The screen shows 'STATUS: 200' immediately for Q2, and the serial log doesn't show any new HTTP request being made for Q2. Can you help me fix this? The Meatloaf source is at /home/qus/dev/_c/meatloaf/.
evals.expected_output: A debugging session that: 1) recognizes this as the known Q2 state machine issue, 2) explains the root cause (session reuse without fresh perform), 3) tries a BASIC-side workaround (close/reopen the channel between requests), 4) if that doesn't work, analyzes the firmware source to find the issue
